Mechanism of action
There are membrane receptors for each type of eicosanoid, which have been studied especially in platelets and smooth muscle. It is
noteworthy that there can be, however, several types of receptors for the same eicosanoid, even in the same cell membrane. In all
cases, membrane signal transduction is carried out by G proteins (Fredriksson and Schioth, 2005). In some cases, stimulation or
inhibition of adenylate cyclase occurs, increasing or decreasing cyclic AMP production. In other cases there is stimulation of phos-
pholipase C, with a consequent increase in diacylglycerols and phosphoinositol bisphosphate. Leukotrienes appear to act through
stimulation of phospholipase C, while PGI2 (prostacyclin) and prostaglandins D and F activate adenylate cyclase.
On the other hand, PGE2 and thromboxane A2 (TXA2), as well as isoprostanes, oxidized derivatives of eicosanoids, can act
through both systems. The action of TXA2 occurs through its TP receptor that interacts with different G proteins, which causes
